market_context: United States; FDA/FoodSafety.gov one-week refrigerated storage guidance
title: How long do hard-boiled eggs last in the fridge?

seo.title: How long do hard-boiled eggs last in the fridge?
seo.meta_description: Hard-boiled eggs keep for up to 1 week in the refrigerator at 40°F or below. Refrigerate within 2 hours and store peeled eggs covered.
seo.search_intent: Find the safe refrigerator storage time for hard-boiled eggs, peeled or unpeeled, and learn how to store them.

excerpt: Hard-boiled eggs can be refrigerated for up to 1 week, peeled or still in the shell, according to FDA guidance. Keep the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below and refrigerate the eggs within 2 hours of cooking. The shell generally protects moisture and texture better; peeled eggs should stay in a clean covered container.
content_html:
Hard-boiling an egg does not make it shelf-stable. It is still a perishable food and still needs refrigeration. The simple rule is up to one week in the refrigerator, provided the eggs were cooled and refrigerated promptly.

One week, assuming the time-and-temperature history is good

That window assumes the eggs were cooked properly, did not spend hours on the counter and stayed in a refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below.

If you cook a batch, date the container. Smell and appearance cannot tell you how many days an egg has been stored.

The shell usually protects quality better

A cooked shell does not make an egg safe on its own, but it does slow moisture loss, reduce direct handling and limit exposure to refrigerator odors. If you do not need to peel the eggs ahead of time, leaving the shells on usually preserves texture better.

Peeled eggs: same window, more protection needed

Once peeled, the egg is directly exposed to air and hands. Keep it in a clean covered container rather than loose on a refrigerator shelf.

It may dry out sooner than a shell-on egg even though the same one-week refrigerator guideline applies.

After cooking, cool and refrigerate promptly

Cold running water or an ice bath helps stop carryover cooking and lowers the temperature quickly. Then dry the eggs and refrigerate them; there is no need to leave them on the counter for hours until they feel completely cold.

FDA's general rule for refrigerated perishables is no more than 2 hours at room temperature, shortened to 1 hour when the surrounding temperature is above 90°F (32°C).

Sulfur smell or a green yolk ring does not automatically mean spoilage

Overcooked eggs can smell more sulfurous and develop a green-gray ring around the yolk because iron and sulfur react during cooking. Those are cooking effects, not proof that the egg has spoiled.

A genuinely rotten odor, slime, mold or other obvious deterioration is different. And even a normal-smelling egg should not be kept beyond the recommended window or rescued after spending too long warm.

Picnics and lunch boxes still need cold control

If hard-boiled eggs will not be eaten within about 2 hours, keep them in an insulated bag or cooler with ice packs. On a very hot day, the room-temperature window is shorter.

Freezing usually is not worth it

Whole hard-boiled eggs do not freeze well. The whites can become rubbery and watery after thawing. It is generally better to cook only what you expect to eat during the week.

What to remember

Up to one week in the refrigerator, chilled promptly and stored protected. The shell helps preserve quality; refrigeration is what limits bacterial growth.

If the eggs sat out for hours or you cannot remember when they were cooked, that history matters more than whether they still look normal.

faq.question: How long do unpeeled hard-boiled eggs last?
faq.answer: Up to 1 week in the refrigerator at 40°F or below.

faq.question: How long do peeled hard-boiled eggs last?
faq.answer: FDA gives the same one-week refrigerated window, but peeled eggs should be stored covered and may dry out sooner.

faq.question: Can I eat a hard-boiled egg left out overnight?
faq.answer: No. Refrigerated perishables should not sit at room temperature for more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F.
